issue.title: mavsdk.pc forces bundled private dependencies on shared-library consumers
issue.body:
### Problem

The generated `mavsdk.pc` declares implementation dependencies as pkg-config private requirements:

```pkgconfig
Requires.private: libcurl jsoncpp tinyxml2
```

(Current `main` uses `nlohmann_json` instead of `jsoncpp`, but retains the same structure.)

For the prebuilt shared-library packages, these dependencies are bundled into `libmavsdk.so`. They are not exposed through MAVSDK's installed public headers and are not dynamic dependencies of the installed shared object. Nevertheless, pkg-config attempts to resolve the private modules when compiler flags are requested.

On a clean Debian 13 ARM64 system with MAVSDK 3.17.2 installed:

```console
$ pkg-config --modversion mavsdk
3.17.2

$ pkg-config --libs mavsdk
-lmavsdk

$ pkg-config --cflags mavsdk
Package libcurl was not found in the pkg-config search path.
Package 'libcurl', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'jsoncpp', required by 'mavsdk', not found
Package 'tinyxml2', required by 'mavsdk', not found
```

This prevents the conventional command from working:

```sh
c++ example.cpp $(pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk)
```

CMake consumers using `find_package(MAVSDK)` build and run successfully on the same system.

### Package inspection

I reproduced this while producing and testing a Debian 13 ARM64 build from the v3.17.2 tag, and also confirmed that the official v3.17.2 Debian 13 AMD64 package contains the same `Requires.private` line.

For the ARM64 shared object:

```console
$ readelf -d /usr/lib/libmavsdk.so.3.17.2 | grep NEEDED
Shared library: [libstdc++.so.6]
Shared library: [libm.so.6]
Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
Shared library: [libc.so.6]
```

The installed MAVSDK public headers do not include curl, jsoncpp, or tinyxml2 headers. The package supplies the shared library and no static `libmavsdk.a`.

### Expected behavior

Installing the shared-library development package should be sufficient for:

```sh
pkg-config --cflags --libs mavsdk
```

Private implementation dependencies already incorporated into `libmavsdk.so` should not require their development packages on the consumer system.

### Suggested fix

Remove `Requires.private` from `mavsdk.pc` for shared-library builds/packages, or generate it conditionally only for a static installation whose final consumer genuinely needs those external archives.

This is related to #2475, which covers the separate hard-coded CI-prefix problem in the generated pkg-config file.

comments.body: Verified against current `main` after filing: HEAD is `46d217875d19179c8266d5545eadcf9978879416` (2026-07-23), and `cpp/src/mavsdk.pc.in` still contains `Requires.private: libcurl nlohmann_json tinyxml2`. The template history shows that #2918 changed the JSON implementation from jsoncpp to nlohmann/json, but did not remove or conditionalize the private pkg-config requirements. Therefore this is still present upstream and is not specific to the v3.17.2 release branch.

> For the prebuilt shared-library packages, these dependencies are bundled into libmavsdk.so

Do you mean for the `.deb` packages for instance? I would argue that they shouldn't be bundled and instead the mavsdk package should rely on the system dependencies 🤔

@JonasVautherin 

Yes, I agree.  I was building a release for debian 13 / Arm64, since there's not one on the release page.  I noticed that it brings in its own ssl, json, tinxyxml, curl, xz, and a few others and on debian at least, those should probably come from the repositories since they're standard packages.

The cmake superbuild part of the build system already has find_package calls to the right parts. I see that -DSUPERBUILD=OFF can control that part already, but it appears to be all or nothing.  The packages available from debian are curl, jsoncpp (and nlohmancpp for the upcoming 4 change), tinyxml2, xz, and openssl.  The other mavlink parts would still need to be built from source, just as they are now, but that's not a big deal, if the user builds the deb package from source.

I'm just throwing around ideas, but perhaps the superbuild option could become just a bit more fine-grained so that the packages available from debian can be skipped on the build side with another option

option( MAVSDK_USE_SYSTEM_COMMON_DEPS   "Use system curl, jsoncpp, tinyxml2, and liblzma"  OFF )

and then always build the specific parts

build_target(mavlink)
build_target(libevents)
build_target(picosha2)
build_target(libmavlike)

and use the option to guard off the debian parts 

if(NOT MAVSDK_USE_SYSTEM_COMMON_DEPS)
    build_target(tinyxml2)
    build_target(jsoncpp)
    build_target(liblzma)
    if(NOT BUILD_WITHOUT_CURL)
        build_target(openssl)
        build_target(zlib-ng)
        build_target(curl)
    endif()
endif()

This would be pretty minimal surgery, since the right structure is in place with the calls to find_package.  The build depends part of the package would probably look something like this 

Build-Depends:
 debhelper-compat (= 13),
 cmake (>= 3.22.1),
 ninja-build,
 pkgconf,
 libcurl4-openssl-dev,
 libjsoncpp-dev,
 libtinyxml2-dev,
 liblzma-dev

and then a small of other debian platform specific changes to the debian rules/control.  Right now the packages are generated, and very useful, but they seem to mix a few paradigms, and could probably be a little more robust with just a few tweaks.

Thanks, 

Kyle B
I'm taking a stab at implementing a series of changes for this that I'm going to create a PR for.  I'm assuming that debian 11 is going to be dropped from V4.

My concern is that it adds complexity to the CMake setup. The goal of making the superbuild optional was that instead of supporting all possible use-cases, we would let advanced users handle dependencies themselves.

Ideally, MAVSDK upstream would not maintain distro packages. In my opinion it is the role of package maintainers to do that for their distro. It's impossible for MAVSDK upstream to properly maintain packages for all distros. In this case, I feel like the reason you need this mix between system libraries and vendored libraries is that mavlink, libevent, picosha2 and libmavlike are not `.deb` packages themselves (and mavlink especially is fundamentally difficult to standardise as a `.deb`, which complicates matters). Actually, [ideally we would not even provide a superbuild](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-superbuild/).

On the other hand, we need a superbuild because most users don't know how to [handle dependencies themselves](https://www.acarg.ch/posts/cmake-deps/) 🤷.

I guess I just don't have a good solution for that 🙈.

I understand your dilemma, I maintain a software package that is something of a vcpkg like entity that uses a superbuild system for dependency management, so I'm very familiar with the hybridization that ends up happening.  

I worked on it some last night, and I think there is a solution that will work without modifying too much of the code.  I believe you were on the right track as it was, I saw some attempt at separating those debian dependencies out.  I'll update in a bit.  

Thanks,

Kyle

Just for the record. I've removed jsoncpp in favor of nlohmann::json in main/v4.

Edit: nevermind, you already mention that.
